title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 119
paragraphs: As for the Eretrians who had been reduced to slavery, when Datis and Artaphernes reached Asia they brought them up to Susa. King Darius, though he had raged against the Eretrians before their capture because they had wronged him without provocation, treated them no more harshly once he saw them in his power as prisoners. He settled them as colonists in the Cissian country on one of his own estates, a place called Ardericca, two hundred and ten stades from Susa and forty stades from the well that yields three kinds of substance: asphalt, salt, and oil, drawn up in the following manner. The liquid is brought up by a sweep, to which half a skin has been fastened in place of a bucket; a man plunges this into the well, draws it up, and pours it into a cistern, from which it runs off in three separate channels. The asphalt and salt solidify at once; the oil — which the Persians call rhadinace — is black and gives off a disagreeable smell. Here King Darius settled the Eretrians, and down to my own day they still occupy this land and keep their original language. So much, then, for what happened to the Eretrians.
